| Completed short rest | Clears protected disablement only | Actual completed short-rest marker |
| Long-rest Drone rebuild | Full HP, fresh physical instance for owned asset, even after old material consumed; preserves uncleared asset disablement | Actual source-authorized completed long rest |

**NEW machine viability arithmetic:** explicit half-maximum reconstruction has minimum 1 HP. Repair Pulse on a functional max-1-HP machine still restores floor(1/2) = 0.

The two ten-minute procedures are distinct rights. Reconstructing a disabled, destroyed Drone does not also buy disable clearance. Reconstruction is not a generic cleanse and does not reset ammunition, modules, spent uses, Overdrive history or unexpired legal effects. Normally damage has already consumed temp HP before destruction; this package adds no destroyed-machine temp-HP grant.

Routing Dissonance is the engine[7] BA, once/short rest, up to two current Dissonance into an active device within 30 feet. It creates no RP, does not reset Refrain, and blocks movement, attacks, auras and triggers while the device's timer continues.

## Capacity, placement and dependent Totems

Deployable slots are zero before the engine's class gate, one at Tinker 6, two at 13 and three at 17. Advanced Turret Bay uses two available slots for 4 RP, or its one-slot/2-RP fallback; zero free slots is illegal. Drones use separate persistent ownership capacity, not deployable slots.

At Tinker 13, choose exactly two basic Drones with exactly one module each or exactly one Drone with exactly two distinct modules during the printed configuration procedure. No more than two. Earlier module acquisition remains governed by its own class gates. **NEW:** withdrawing the excess Drone into an unavailable/retracted configuration causes no destruction or salvage.

Totem capacity is one, then two at Shaman 13. **NEW generalization:** an ordinary new Totem placed at capacity replaces a chosen active Totem, including at capacity one. Echo needs a separate free capacity; creating Echo alone never evicts another Totem.

**NEW dependent Echo rule:** ending, replacing, destroying or expiring the parent ends its Echo and releases both capacities. That Echo ending is administrative, not its own destruction. Ending only Echo leaves the parent. Echo shares the parent's remaining duration, concentration and upkeep.

Preflight ownership, source use, space/range, action, resources and capacity before payment or ending anything. Determine all dependent releases first. A valid parent replacement can free room for the new parent plus a separately paid Echo. If Echo cannot fit, its optional creation is unavailable; the caller can submit an ordinary parent-only placement instead. Failure of a submitted combined transaction changes nothing.

All active Totems share their concentration burden. Losing it ends their effects and dependent Echoes without destruction rewards. Totem movement follows its printed BA, 15-foot move through an open route within the printed range; it retains expiry, concentration, recipient ledgers and pulse schedule. Movement grants no entry heal.

## Destruction, debris and source-specific opportunities

Record the instance, original hostile cause, actual enemy hit versus transferred damage, deliberate sacrifice, whether the object itself is a copy, friendly damage, secondary explosion and inherited branch flags at destruction. Separately record whether incoming damage was copied. A real device destroyed by copied damage still has ordinary destruction consequences; only that damage's actual restriction flags suppress them. “Copied object” exclusions do not mean “any object damaged by a copy.”

**NEW anti-loop integration:** the first actual destruction of an instance establishes its only object-linked opportunity and material set. Nonqualifying and declined opportunities are closed for that instance. Snap does not create another set. A second physical destruction still ends the rebuilt device but cannot supply another harvest, Volatile opportunity or material record.

Recycling, Salvage, Reaper and Snap share the usable original material. The first successful consumer spends it. Volatile does not consume material. A source-qualified Volatile can therefore precede one legal material consumer. Declining Volatile on Device A does not spend the owner's round allowance for Device B.

| Source | Important predicate |
| --- | --- |
| Efficient Recycling | Your destroyed non-copy device; not deliberate sacrifice; debris within reach, after combat for one minute, 1/short rest. Refund at most min(1 RP, actual deployment RP). Enemy cause is **not required**. |
| Scrap Salvage | Enemy-destroyed qualifying material; Action+1 RP, 1/encounter; one slot-using Scrapling at printed location |
| Scrap Reaper | Qualifying destroyed enemy-hit device/material within 30 feet; Reaction+2 RP, 1/short rest; printed short-lived Scrapling uses **no deployable slot** |
| Volatile Components | First enemy-caused device destruction; excludes deliberate sacrifice, copy, friendly damage and secondary explosion; enemy within 5 feet; once per owner/round |
| Snap | Original destroyed instance/material, original footprint free and original expiry not reached |

Scraplings cannot spawn their own replacement. Reaper still uses the later BA command and damaging-action budget for its detonation. Its absent slot cost is not inferred from the separate Salvage card. Reaper also carries its source's broader no-own-destruction-chain property; a later type ruling must not silently remove that protection.

Inherited noResourceGeneration blocks Recycling refunds. It does not automatically prohibit all non-resource transformations. Inherited noRetaliation blocks a destruction explosion such as Volatile. Inherited noDeathTriggers blocks Volatile, Cinder's destruction burst and Reaper's destruction-triggered Reaction. It does not automatically prohibit the later Action-based Scrap Salvage or ordinary Recycling. Source-specific exclusions still apply to each consumer.

Cinderflame's qualifying destruction event is captured before its standard-companion disappearance. Its printed burst may then resolve, with the printed three-enemy cap, save, damage and no further death/resource triggers. Dismissal, expiry and concentration ending are not destruction.

Volatile Injection spends M **normal** device HP and requires current HP strictly greater than M. Temp HP cannot pay it. It is not damage or a qualifying destruction event. Deliberate sacrifice sources retain their express no-proc/salvage/copy/refund exclusions.

## Magnetic Wall and existing damage sharing

**NEW source binding and timing integration:** when the printed ranged weapon hit, ally distance and wall-line predicates hold, the owner's Reaction transfers exactly min(remaining defended damage, S+M) to the functional Wall after the ally's ordinary defenses/prevention and before temp HP.

The transfer retains damage type. The Wall branch carries noSecondMitigation and noRetransfer. It receives no second AC roll, critical, attack-hit rider or second mitigation pass. Legal Wall temp HP then normal HP absorb it; reaching zero destroys it and releases its slot.

Enemy damage intercepted this way remains enemy-caused. Choosing the Reaction is not deliberate sacrifice. A Wall destroyed this way may qualify Volatile and a source-qualified material consumer. Transferred damage is not itself an attack hit on the Wall; enemy-hit-only Reaper qualification remains distinct.

Emergency Protocols retains its existing additional noRetaliation flag. Enemy attribution and ordinary debris survive, but destroying the Drone cannot bypass that flag to trigger Volatile. This new Magnetic Wall binding supplements the earlier 39-source redirection package; it was not part of that package's original count.

## Reconfiguration and implementation boundaries

Reconfiguration requires a functional deployed device and a known eligible nonhealing destination. **NEW arithmetic:** newHP = max(1, floor(oldHP × newMaxHP / oldMaxHP)), capped at new max. Preserve instance, slot footprint, expiry, ammunition, spent uses, destruction history and effect clocks. This conversion is neither damage nor healing.

Pending modifiers only apply when their own predicate remains true. Overcharge grants no free command; a profile unable to use it does not refund it or reset its deadline. Exact source access, profile legality and pending-modifier application remain caller responsibilities.

Restoration Field is a slot-using concentration effect with its already-reviewed healing scheduler. Its source supplies no HP, AC or physical anchor. It cannot be attacked as a fabricated machine, repaired, Snap Rebuilt, Remote Detonated, used for Volatile Injection/salvage or targeted by protected Dissonance routing merely because it consumes a slot.

The implementation stores authoritative owner/instance/material identifiers, original ClockMarkers, canonical command ledgers, atomic RP/action payments and explicit source-scoped use keys. The caller must provide the same real owner wallet and ledger across abilities, unique use-scope keys tied to the real rest/encounter calendar, legal source actions and costs, actual targets/geometry, source profiles and class gates. It must also propagate these life states to the pulse/concentration engine.

All timed device effects supplied here expire during a completed long rest, explaining the fresh Drone instance's empty timed-effect list and zero tempHP. This is not a generic reconstruction cleanse: a future permanent or long-rest-surviving source effect must retain its own clock and rules.

This reference does not create a complete runtime transaction manager, movement/collision system, all damage riders, every condition interaction, all 157 remaining companion candidates or a video game. It supplies the same decisions in tabletop prose and a precise checked model for later implementation.

# Creature companions: life, commands and identity

**REVIEWED / reference-VALIDATED: 121 targeted checks and 2,800 Ranger conversion states.** This overlay discusses 100 exact passages from Druid, Mage, Mirrorsage, Ranger and Wizard, supported by five frozen common paragraphs. It closes no full class, form, temporary-HP system or complete runtime by itself. [Source register](CREATURE_LIFECYCLE_SOURCE_BINDINGS.md), [source integrity](CREATURE_LIFECYCLE_SOURCE_VALIDATION.json), [behavior checks](CREATURE_LIFECYCLE_PLAYTEST_VALIDATION.json).

The original class cards and frozen class guide remain intact. The notebook's first classification, boundary reconciliation and event-model decisions are preserved in the audit folder. Where the historical first reply differs from the later boundary replies, the later explicit resolution controls. In particular, Auto-Raise is automatic, its new minion cannot act at all in the creation round, and Mirrorsage Charm was not in the older 219-source control closure.

## At the table

Keep one companion command and one offensive companion allowance per owner per numbered round, including multiclass companions and devices. A normal command costs your Bonus Action. A damaging companion action, or Mage/Wizard control action, spends the offensive allowance. A pure support command spends only the command. The earlier device ledger's internal field named `damage` now represents this shared offensive allowance; its public behavior remains compatible with existing device checks.

Issue ordinary commands during your regular turn. The selected companion moves and performs its command immediately after your whole turn, in an attached phase. It receives no extra independent turn. If it or its target becomes ineligible before execution, the command fails without refund. Your later incapacity or removal alone does not cancel an issued command; actual concentration/source ending can. Uncommanded companions can move defensively and Dodge, subject to their conditions; this grants no generic Reaction or autonomous attack/control.

Use the owner's original regular companion markers for recharge and previous/next-turn references. Extra turns, initiative changes and removal do not restart those markers. The attached phase's event-resolution checkpoint is distinct: it refreshes no Reaction, recharge, Action, death save or regular duration clock.

## Different kinds of creature life

| Creature | HP and 0 HP | Return and identity |
|---|---|---|
| Finite standard summons, Druid swarms, Mage Familiar, Mirror Beasts | HP-only bounded layer; at 0 disappear/end | No corpse, resource or free resummon; a new summon pays its actual source costs |
| Ranger Beast | HP-only; **NEW** immediate death at 0, no Wound checks, Stable or death saves | Actual animal and ordinary surviving corpse; death ends bond. No automatic resurrection or rebond |
| Mage Lich elite | Destroyed bound asset at 0; no usable corpse/resources | Same unique asset remains owned. Soulbound or actual completed LR can return it |
| Wizard standard undead | Destroyed at 0; consumed body never returns as new fuel | Ends on destruction, dismissal or owner's next completed LR, including Auto-Raised minions |
| Wizard elite | Supplied profile/cap only in this package | Binding/acquisition and return procedure are still missing; no create/bind/return API |
| Reflective Companion | Original creature's HP and life rules | Temporary control relation; no copied body, reset, new statistics or duplicate turn |
| Druid form | Same character's HP/life rules | Full forms and Buffer Reserve remain a separate open interface |

Companion healing restores legal normal HP only. It does not reset identity, duration, recharge, actions, source uses, effects or command budgets. Ranger's “heal normally” supplies no Hit Dice pool or automatic rest healing. The HP-only layer is specific to this reviewed companion chassis, not generic law for all animals/NPCs. Existing animal conditions, disease, poison, explicit injuries and timed effects survive bonding.

## Stats and ownership

**NEW:** finite created creatures snapshot base HP and AC at creation. Attacks, saves, class DC and S use the current values of the original source owner at resolution. Keep source owner, current controller, source class and creation source separate. A temporary controller does not donate their class levels, PB or attack bonus. The implementation rejects stats belonging to another owner/class; it provides no unrestricted transfer/rebinding operation.

Standard profile: AC 12 + floor(PB/2), HP 2L, Speed 30, owner PB for saves, one class attack for S d6 with printed melee/ranged mode. Druid swarm uses current PB+WIS, piercing and its printed tiny-gap movement. Familiar snapshots AC 12+PB and HP 5+Mage level+M; its current source-owner Mage attack fires a 30-foot Elemental Dart for S d4. Focus is fixed at creation: Lightning adds Fly30, Fire/Cold their matching resistance. Changing Focus neither morphs nor refills it. One Familiar; replacement ends the prior one.

Ranger maximum is **NEW dynamic** max(1, 2×current Ranger level + actual WIS modifier), not M. Current PB updates its standard AC/saves/attack. Persistent Mage elite maxima use current source-owner Mage level; fixed AC stays fixed. Capacity growth never heals; shrink clamps HP without damage. Wizard elite profiles use the same names with their own original Wizard source statistics if a future legitimate binding source establishes them.

The [reviewed maximum-HP ledger](MAXIMUM_HP_PLAYTEST.md) supplies source-qualified modifiers. Conjuration is the original creating Wizard level snapshot and requires actual Wizard spell creation. Corpse Harvest qualifies only with actual access; Auto-Raise is not a spell and grants no new Conjuration snapshot. Flesh Ascendant is the explicit dynamic eligible-current-controller exception; engine and card are one effect, not two bonuses. Creation starts at full final legal maximum unless the actual source enters damaged; later added capacity never fills HP. Callers update dynamic modifier records from their real sources.

## Ranger's persistent bond

Use the printed one-hour ritual, touch, 4 RP and one long-rest use. The animal must already be willing/tamed, noncorrupted, INT below7 and CR no greater than Ranger level. The helper does not invent finding/taming rules. Keep one chosen movement mode, capped40 feet, and the original keen-sense identity; no monster stat block, boss powers or free special actions. Exact keen-sense selection definitions remain an evidence gap.

**NEW initial conversion:** for a living animal, new HP = max(1, floor(new maximum × old current HP / old maximum)). A wounded animal stays proportionally wounded. This is profile conversion, not healing or damage. A living bound Beast cannot be rebonded to refill HP. On death, ordinary legal resurrection may restore the same animal under its own source, but it remains unbonded. A new full ritual also requires an actual completed long rest after bond death.

Physical body identity is separate from current corpse eligibility. Keep one record whose state is living, corpse, consumed or removed. Accepting an already-resolved, independently legal resurrection immediately marks that same body living and unavailable as a corpse, before any rebond. Corpse Gateway cannot use it while living. A later genuine death with a surviving body makes that same record a corpse again; no fragment/new body identity is generated. A consumed/removed body requires explicit reconstruction by the actual resurrection source before it can return. The notification helper grants no resurrection ability, payment exemption or automatic bond. Rebond uses the actual post-resurrection HP ratio and preserves death history; it cannot claim a healthier ratio. Full global corpse decay/cleanup remains open.

## Mage Lich assets and elite commands

An actual successful Lich transformation unlocks Boneflayer, Dreadblade and Wraithbound. Readiness and informed retirement-risk consent are source guards; this lifecycle helper does not perform that irreversible ritual. **NEW shared identity:** across Mage/Wizard, one owner can have at most one of each named elite and three total. Destroyed assets still occupy those identities. Any future external Wizard binding must validate against the same asset register; the current helper offers only its profile schema.

| Elite | Profile | Source-native actions/riders |
|---|---|---|
| Boneflayer | AC14, HP12+2L, Speed30; ranged60, 2d6+S necrotic | Fear Pulse replaces attack, enemies10 feet WIS or Frightened through target-next-end, recharge3. Grave Miasma replaces attack: radius10 point30 until next owner-start, enemies entry/start1d6 once, recharge3 |
| Dreadblade | AC16, HP16+3L, Speed30; melee5, 1d8+S necrotic | Concentrating hit target immediately saves with disadvantage; natural20 applies printed −1 attack Weakened until target-next-end. Advantage against forced movement |
| Wraithbound | AC14, HP10+2L, Fly40/hover; melee5, 1d8+S necrotic | Natural20 CON or Stunned until target-next-end under shared character→target hard-denial guard |

Rolls, chosen enemy geometry, recharge payments, exact condition applications and canonical hard-guard sharing remain caller/source responsibilities. This helper returns attack profiles and bounded lifecycle/command transitions; it does not silently execute every on-hit effect.

**NEW Miasma integration:** creation spends one offensive command. Its native finite entry/start damage needs no second command and does not spend next round's offense. Retain no-resource/no-recursion flags. An old zone tick is not a new companion turn or attack.

Wraithbound loses source invisibility on attack **or control**. It can regain it at the end of its next original regular companion marker if the predicate remains satisfied. A current-marker end cannot immediately restore it. The actual offense event must notify its marker state. Core Invisible still does not grant unknown location, sight through walls or automatic target legality.

Soulbound requires the destroyed own bound elite within30 or its inert token, legal empty space30, Action, 5 RP and one LR use. Return the same asset/instance at **NEW source-specific** max(1, floor(current maximum/2)), plus S+M temp HP for60 seconds under normal temp-HP rules. Do not copy machine reconstruction permissions. Preserve spent uses, recharge clocks, command history and still-applicable effects. Completed LR returns those same Mage assets at full current HP unless an actual campaign consequence prevents it. Rest-use/recharge resets come only from the canonical rest system; a return itself grants none. Natural effect expiries must still be processed.

## Wizard corpses, standard minions and Auto-Raise

Corpse Harvest costs Action+4 RP, recharge2, legal corpse/space30. Humanoids qualify; actual Infernal Pact also permits Fiends. Skeleton: AC14, HP6+2WizardL, Speed30, ranged30 1d6+S necrotic. Zombie: AC12, HP10+3L, Speed20, melee5 1d8+S. Goblin Thrall: AC13, HP8+2L, Speed30, melee5 1d6+S; requires a goblinoid body even with Pact.

All standard minions and reserved Auto-Raise slots share a cap of3. Manually dismiss an existing standard minion before attempting a fourth; failed creation spends nothing and does not consume the body. Harvest consumes the original body. Summoned, raised, copied, illusory or fragmented remains provide no new corpse fuel. Corpse Gateway uses a legal body without consuming it; it does not grant raising permission. Global corpse decay/removal rules remain open.

Ghoul Lash uses the shared BA command and2 RP with another controlled undead within5 at issuance. Its chosen standard minion makes **two independently rolled normal attacks**, not numerical damage copies. Each can miss/hit/crit. This remains one command and one offensive allowance, with at most one Auto-Raise opportunity.

**NEW queue integration, preserving the printed automatic trigger:** the first qualifying personal killing blow by a standard minion automatically reserves the body, one capacity slot and the killer's mechanical minion type. It spends the owner's round opportunity immediately. Ineligible kills do not spend it; a qualifying trigger cannot voluntarily be declined. Body reservation does not prevent another legal consumer from taking the body first. A destroyed/expired killer does not cancel an already-created reservation.

Resolve after immediate death responses and already-due end damage/saves, before ordinary expiry cleanup, in stable application order. An ordinary attached attack has its own `attachedCompanionEnd` queue checkpoint after its consequences, in the same numbered round. That checkpoint is not a second regular turn marker. Kills before the checkpoint closes may reserve. A later administrative kill cannot reopen it, roll forward or leave an orphan queue; its unused opportunity remains unused unless another independently valid trigger occurs before another legally open checkpoint.

At resolution, still-eligible body, legal space and cap permit creation; otherwise release the reservation but retain the spent round use. Auto-Raise costs no Action or RP. The newborn cannot voluntarily move, Dodge, support, attack, control or react in its creation numbered round. Passive defenses/conditions/expiry continue. It ends at destruction, dismissal or next completed owner LR. Owner unconsciousness/death alone does not invent a new ending.

## Mirror Beast, Reflective Companion and Echo origin

One Mirror Beast **or** Reflective Companion slot. Summoning a Beast replaces the old body/control relation administratively; it never kills the real previously controlled target. Mirrorcall adds M max/current HP at creation and5 Speed. Advanced Mirrorcall spends BA once/encounter for appearance plus its printed swim/climb adjustment; Mirror Shift spends BA+1 RP/recharge2 for swim30 or climb30. Neither heals, restores uses, releases Echoes, grants flight/anatomy, or refreshes duration. Corrupted and Shattered on-hit dice/splash retain their exact once-round source qualifiers; full damage-event execution remains in the later copy/trigger work. Luminant Bond supplies only its printed local WIS-save/Invisible advantage interface, with ordinary cover/targeting intact.

Ordinary Beast: Action2 RP, empty space15, one minute, recharge3. Radiant/Shattered: Action4 RP, empty space15, concentration3 of the owner's regular turns, recharge4. Actual scheduler supplies the precise three-turn endpoint. Radiant chooses attack, BA+1 RP heal S d4 to living ally5, or paid Echo origin, once per numbered round. The healing pipeline resolves rolls/modifiers before the lifecycle HP gain; no invented resurrection.

**NEW Mirror-origin exception:** your Echo resolves immediately as your Action during your own turn, including a real extra own turn if real Action, BA and unused shared caps exist. An extra Action alone supplies no BA. Preflight active Beast, actual record, release cap, owner target perception, current Beast range/LOE, Action, BA and RP before any spend. The Beast grants no remote sensory feed or free preceding movement. You own record consumption, Dissonance, Refrain, concentration and spell damage. BA command is spent; offensive companion allowance is not. A later independently legal Gadget Sync may spend it. No second BA command or second local Beast option appears.

Charm Creature remains Action3 RP, one LR use, WIS save, target INT<=6 within30, concentration at most3 rounds, no PC/boss without actual encounter permission. Repeat save at target's actual turn end and when harmed by your side. No suicide, compelled beliefs or permanent allegiance. Original identity/HP/conditions/effects/stat provenance/initiative remain unchanged. A successful save spends cast costs but does not replace an existing Beast. Source-specific save/Charm immunity and permitted target/route checks remain caller responsibilities.

**NEW hard-denial reconciliation:** initial Charm applies the actual Charmed relation and slot without spending hard denial. While active, one BA may queue at most one pending forced ordinary Action, never unique powers; ordinary attack damage capped S d6. Queue to the next future regular target Action: this round if upcoming, next round if already passed. Pay BA in issue round; reserve offensive allowance in the resolution round. The target receives no duplicate attached turn.

At the designated Action slot, revalidate Charm, capability, legal order and the shared character→target→encounter hard guard. Valid execution replaces that Action and spends both hard guard and offense. If Charm ends, target becomes incapable, legality fails or another same-character feature spends hard denial, cancel and release unused offense; retain BA/costs and do not spend an additional hard denial. Call the pending-order revalidation when those facts change, not only at the future turn. Once a forced Action has occurred, this effect permits no further forced attack, Dodge, movement or replacement Action. Actual Charmed restrictions/repeat saves remain; no new fallback is invented.

## Druid summon dependencies

Base Swarm Summoning: Action, one SR use, space30, concentration10 minutes; independent of form. Carrion Rat King: Action, actual Form Surge, once per shift, one standard swarm for at most60 seconds and only while its parent form remains; replacement affects its old form swarm, not independent Base Swarm. Broodmother: on entry actual Form Surge creates two adjacent bodies with one combined commanded attack; end at the earlier of60 seconds or parent form end. Form change ends those children, not unrelated paid summons.

Master of Vermin substitutes the paid summoning spell's profile while preserving its actual count, duration and concentration. No extra casts, creatures or command budget. Its independently paid spell creatures do not inherit a form-ending dependency solely from that substitution. Full forms, reserve arithmetic, per-form special actions and temporary-HP effects remain open.

## Reference boundaries and next work

The helper requires certified source access, legal target/space/range/LOE/perception, ordinary condition capability, real paid Form Surge, canonical action wallets/use scopes, actual concentration/clock endpoints and actual completed rest events. These are explicit inputs, not guessed by creature names. A fresh wallet/ledger per ability is invalid integration. Recharge/frequency keys represent already validated canonical scopes; caller must not mint a new key to bypass them.

Open: Wizard elite binding/return, real Beast natural rest and keen-sense details, global corpse cleanup, broader companion families, full forms/tempHP, complete damage/copy/proc execution, ordinary spell and content catalogs, human balance and complete runtime. Classification of incidental source passages is not closure of their complete effects.

[Final notebook disposition](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_CREATURE_LIFECYCLE_FINAL_CLOSURE.md) approves only the selected100+5 source roles and interfaces described here. Incidental full-form/tempHP effects remain deferred.


## Dominate Beast integration

The [reviewed rank-three Enchantment supplement](ENCHANTMENT_RANK3_INTEGRATION_PLAYTEST.md) adds the source-qualified Dominate Beast bridge for actual Beast companions. It redirects only an existing owner-attached execution opportunity, preserves original profile/source-owner stats, reuses a same-companion/same-phase pending reservation where applicable, and occupies the original owner's structural command/offense caps without charging that owner's Bonus Action. It grants no independent companion turn, duplicate phase or new resource pool. # Resonance & Dissonance — Canon Magic Economy

**Status:** Canon — consolidated 2026-07-31  
**Player terms:** Resonance, Resonance Points (RP), Resonance Rank, Dissonance, Refrain, Retune, Ground the Note  
**Core principle:** RP limits how much magical power a caster has available. Dissonance limits how recklessly or repetitively that power can be forced through the Weave.

## 1. Metaphysical rule

Aethel and the Weave are resonant structures. Life, death, memory, motion, elemental force, prayer, blood, and thought all carry pattern. Spellcasting is the act of sounding one of those patterns strongly enough that the Weave reproduces it.

Magic therefore has two simultaneous limits:

1. **Resonance Points** — remaining power and endurance.
2. **Dissonance** — accumulated phase strain between caster, spell, and Weave.

A caster can still have RP and nevertheless be too dissonant to cast safely. This is intentional and prevents a caster from solving every encounter by repeating one efficient spell until the pool is empty.

## 2. Resonance Rank and spell overlap

Every named spell has a **Resonance Rank (0–9)**. Rank is the spell pattern's complexity/cost basis, not a universal character-level gate.

Each class has three independent pieces of spell access:

- **School/thread access** — which magical traditions the class can learn.
- **Effective Resonance Rank** — which school/rank placement that class uses when a spell appears in more than one school.
- **Class acquisition level** — the character level at which that class can learn that Rank.

This intentionally uses a class-driven spell-learning model: the same named spell may be shared by several classes while arriving at different character levels. The spell is stored once; its class access is not.

Current catalog contract:

- **936 school/rank placements**
- **848 unique named spells**
- **619 spells currently have more than one class acquisition level**
- **14 general Weave-casting base classes**
- **Oracle:** Revelation Charges, not RP
- **Soldier / Warrior:** no general Weave spell list

See `SPELL_CATALOG_CANON.md`, `class_spell_school_mapping.csv`, and `class_spell_progression.csv`.

## 3. RP pools

All fourteen general Weave-casting base classes have an L1–20 pool curve in `src/data/resonance-economy.js`.

Full casters use the largest pools. Half, hybrid, and minor Weave users have smaller pools because their class-specific engine carries part of their power budget.

The RP pool never replaces a class's unique mechanic.

## 4. Base RP cost

```text
Base RP cost = Resonance Rank × 2
```

Rank 0 cantrips cost **0 RP**.

Only explicit **class or item text** may modify this cost, plus the universal Dissonance surcharge and chosen Overcast options. Moral alignment and faction reputation are never automatic cost modifiers.

## 5. Dissonance

### Dissonance Limit

```text
Dissonance Limit = 2 + Proficiency Bonus + positive casting-ability modifier
minimum 4
```

### Dissonance gained per cast

- Rank 0: **0 base Dissonance**
- Rank 1–5: **+1 base Dissonance**
- Rank 6–9: **+2 base Dissonance**
- Every selected Overcast modification: **+1 Dissonance**
- Casting outside a class feature's explicitly permitted key/thread, when a feature says so: **+1 Dissonance**

### Refrain

Immediate repetition of the same named spell adds additional Dissonance:

- first cast: no Refrain penalty
- first immediate repeat: +1
- second immediate repeat: +2
- third and later immediate repeats: +3 maximum

This applies to cantrips. A cantrip is free in RP, not free in phase strain.

Casting a different named spell breaks Refrain, but does not erase accumulated Dissonance.

## 6. Dissonance states

| State | Threshold | Effect |
|---|---:|---|
| **In Tune** | Below Limit | Normal casting |
| **Frayed** | Limit | +1 RP to ranked spells |
| **Discordant** | Limit +3 | +2 RP; ordinary casters cannot Overcast |
| **Fractured** | Limit +6 | +3 RP; ordinary casters cannot cast Rank 1+ spells |

Fracture is the hard anti-spam cutoff for ordinary Weave casters.

## 7. Restoring harmony

- **Let the Note Fall:** a turn with no spell or Weave ability removes 1 Dissonance.
- **Ground the Note:** spend the action without casting; remove Dissonance equal to Proficiency Bonus.
- **Retune (short rest):** reset Dissonance to 0 and restore the class's short-rest RP amount.
- **Meditation:** optional 10-minute, once/day recovery; reduces Dissonance by PB + positive casting modifier and restores its listed RP amount.
- **Long rest:** restores RP to maximum and Dissonance to 0.

## 8. Class cadence is protected

Resonance is a universal law, not a replacement class mechanic.

| Class | Protected mechanic | Resonance interaction |
|---|---|---|
| Bard | Crescendo | Complete/consume rhythm to vent strain; repeating one spell is not rhythm |
| Cleric | Conviction | Rites/Invocations alter cadence and can vent limited strain |
| Crimson Agent | Blood Gauge / Blood Marks | Routes some strain through blood by spending Gauge |
| Dragoon | Momentum | Movement carries the note and reduces limited Dissonance |
| Druid | Shapeshifting | Changing form changes the body sounding the Weave and clears Refrain |
| Mage | Elemental Focus / Nuke Chains / Resonance Surge | Different elemental spells form chains; completing a chain vents strain |
| Monk | Ki Flow / Stances | Ki can stabilize minor Weave techniques without becoming RP |
| Mirrorsage | Echo Slots / Mirrorbind | First replay of a new Echo is protected; repetition still builds Refrain |
| Oracle | Mystery / Curse / Revelation Charges | No RP or Weave Dissonance; RC + Prophecy Triggers are its anti-spam system |
| Ranger | Track Target / Weapon Synergy | Weapon hits between casts break cadence and stabilize the next spell |
| Shaman | Totems / Elemental Attunement | Totems function as resonators that reduce limited Dissonance |
| Soldier | Palisade / Overwatch | No general Weave casting |
| Thief | Sneak Attack / Poison | Hidden delivery stabilizes limited minor Weave tricks |
| Tinker | Drone / Deployables | Devices may absorb limited Dissonance and then disable |
| Warrior | Mutations / Serum / Brutality | No general Weave casting |
| Wizard | Spell Matrix | Rotating prepared matrices is inherently stable; repetition builds Refrain |
| Paladin | Oath / Smite / Aura / Lay on Hands | Oath powers are not ordinary spell spam; martial cadence stabilizes Oath spells |

The authoritative software contract is `src/data/class-core-mechanics.js`.

## 9. Dark-path exception — Lich and Necromancer

**Lich** and **Necromancer** are intentionally evil exceptions to safe Weave practice.

They do not gain a moral discount. They gain the willingness and technique to **force magic through damage that would stop another caster**.

### Traumatic Casting

A Lich or Necromancer may:

- cast Rank 1+ spells while Fractured;
- Overcast while Discordant or Fractured.

After the spell resolves, the caster takes direct magical trauma based on the resulting Dissonance state:

| State | Backlash |
|---|---:|
| Frayed | 1 × spell Rank |
| Discordant | 2 × spell Rank |
| Fractured | 3 × spell Rank |

Minimum backlash is 1. This is direct metaphysical trauma and is not reduced by ordinary damage resistance.

### Lich — Soul Furnace

Lich remains a **Mage**. Elemental Focus, Nuke Chains, and Resonance Surge remain part of the play loop.

- Soul Reservoir converts death/DoT pressure into Resonance recovery.
- Once per rest, Soul Reservoir can absorb one Traumatic Casting backlash.
- Lich does not "harmonize" Dissonance; it burns souls and selfhood to continue through it.

### Necromancer — Grave Conductor

Necromancer remains a **Wizard**. Spell Matrix preparation and rotation remain part of the play loop.

- Once per round, destroy one controlled undead or consume a fresh corpse within 30 ft to absorb one Traumatic Casting backlash.
- The spell still generates its full Dissonance.
- The corpse/minion is functioning as a disposable resonator, not as free RP.

No other alignment, class, school, or path ignores the Fractured cutoff unless an explicit future rule says so.

## 10. Overcasting and Low Resonance

Overcasting increases effect by paying additional RP **and** additional Dissonance. Current options remain Empowered, Extended, Widened, Heightened, Quickened, Subtle, Distant, and Twinned.

Dropping below **25% of maximum RP** is called **Low Resonance**. It is an informational resource warning, not a second strain subsystem and not an automatic penalty. Dissonance is the universal rule that governs repetitive and reckless casting.

This distinction matters: a caster can have 1 RP and remain perfectly In Tune, or have a nearly full RP pool and still be Fractured from forcing the same pattern again and again.

## 11. Reputation

Reputation changes access to teachers, sanctuaries, focuses, libraries, components, recipes, political protection, and faction-specific training. It does **not** change the intrinsic Resonance Rank of a spell, its base RP cost, a caster's natural RP capacity, or Dissonance merely because a faction likes or hates the caster.

A faction reward can still provide a concrete named benefit—such as a temporary focus, a specialized lesson, or a sanctuary effect—but that benefit must be written explicitly as an item, feature, scene reward, or training benefit.

## 12. Multiclass Resonance

When a hero has multiple Weave-casting classes:


# Time Loop: reviewed foundational transaction kernel

**Status: REVIEWED / reference-VALIDATED within the bounded foundational scope. Full Time Loop remains unavailable.**

**Current-file qualification:** the original approval binds helper hash `b821829ed352e69ce1ecf3c3d753f0206c8f8d2ec5a5d64bc89d5fd7d8a72151`, preserved as `docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/temporal_playtest_rules_reviewed_foundation.py` at the game root. This implements a bounded part of `oracle.supplement.spiral-touched.spiral-touched-boon-v`. It does not change the original source, enable the ability in the playable class catalog, or close the full temporal interface. The notebook's twelve decisions are the authority for this candidate: [boundary conference](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_WORLD_BOUNDARIES.md).

## What is implemented

The reference restores an immutable initiative-start snapshot through a preflighted transaction. It handles a finite development scene containing canonical Core life states, action wallets, selected feat shields, a temporal healing-consumption ledger, explicit Soul Bind/death identities, physical provenance, finite level-ground geometry, reward opportunities, external dependency records and character memory. The existing shared `LifeState`, `Wallet` and `BufferLedger` objects retain their identities. Spent resources and historical event records remain current.

The restore is permitted only after a complete atomic combat event, before round four, with an available Reaction and an unspent actual long-rest use. It never interrupts a damage, healing or command transaction. Preflight checks all registered state, source policies, physical dependencies and placements before charging anything. A prepared plan becomes stale if the registered world changes before commit. The single-thread reference requires the host scene lock through preflight and commit. Each committed restore also retains an engine/Director audit frame with the previous and resulting field values; that audit is never a source of character memory. The existing canonical BufferLedger completed-rest epoch also governs Time Loop's own long-rest use; there is no independent rest counter to diverge.

At commit, encounter initiative and the snapshot's Action/Bonus Action/Reaction allowances, RC and declared per-encounter uses return. Every outstanding Oracle Time Loop Reaction debt overlays the restored budgets. Only the owner's actual normal regular-start refresh clears that owner's debt. The public `TemporalKernel.regular_start(actor, now)` obtains the actor's canonical Wallet internally; it accepts no Wallet argument and rejects actor aliases sharing one Wallet. The bounded scheduler enforces the next actor at the initiative cursor, allows one active regular turn, and advances the cursor/round only when that exact turn ends. An out-of-order or repeated start cannot refresh a Reaction or advance the actual regular marker. Genuine extra turns require the later source adapter and cannot be represented as regular starts. The new iteration has fresh round/turn identities; the rewind itself creates no turn start, pulse or recharge tick. Elapsed world time, real regular-marker count, RP and finite-use history remain unchanged.

## Conservation checks

| State | Bounded behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Core HP and Wounds | Restore numeric snapshot HP against the current legal maximum. A lower maximum clamps HP without damage or healing; a higher maximum does not increase snapshot HP. Critical Wound healing ceilings do not limit temporal assignment. |
| Maximum HP | Use the existing maximum-HP calculation and an exact source-ID temporal policy table. The three reviewed Monk trauma IDs may restore except after actual rest ending. Tough, Tough as Nails, Tenacity and Dark Fortitude use current permanent progression records; temporary endpoints on those passive records are rejected. Other sources, including valid ordinary max-HP sources whose temporal/lifecycle adapter is absent, reject this fixture. Current supported external records overlay the result. Structural progression changes reject without a dedicated adapter. The host supplies current legal base/stat values. |
| Stable recovery | Preserve its original world deadline and event identity. An already resolved or expired recovery cannot replay; this kernel rejects such restoration rather than inventing a recovery rule. |
| Temporary HP | Restore the same grant ID and original snapshot amount only while its source's deadline/rest epoch/entity dependency remains valid. Supported IDs are Chef, Inspiring Leader, Field Medic, Soul Cage, Empowered Summoning and Blood Ritual. Required canonical ledger fields, unique grant IDs, active target/state and positive remaining amount are validated. Unknown sources and linked riders reject the scene. |
| One-shot healing reduction | Keep canonical effect ID and all past events. Consumption keys include the iteration. Snapshot-available Agony can be available in a new iteration before its original expiry; snapshot-consumed or expired Agony remains unavailable. |
| Soul Bind | Original absolute deadline, exact death instance for bound-dead records. An active pending record requires a living, non-Stable, dying zero-HP target with no death-instance binding. Application and target identities must match. Undoing a later death removes that later active bind. No revival event or source cost is manufactured. |
| Rewards | A claim belongs to encounter origin, immutable reward source, opportunity kind and source-defined slot. Another death event or iteration cannot make another claim. |
| Physical derivatives | Traverse immutable provenance transitively. A wholly in-scope, reversible temporal entity can retire; its costs stay spent. Surviving harvested inventory, mixed material roots, external source slots or persistent enrollment conflicts block the restore. Already consumed material remains consumed. |
| Outsiders | Keep body state, inventory ownership, resource history and concentration records. A snapshot dependency must still exist exactly and refer to the same live concentration ID. New current dependencies targeting restored participants need a supported overlay; otherwise they block. Unimplemented external anatomy/control/suppression overlays also block. |
| Environment | Each anchor has an exact canonical physical identity. Restore snapshot environment existence together with its geometry; remove both the physical derivative and its geometry when retiring a later temporal entity. Plan all participant positions simultaneously. Reject overlap, loss of support, and restrictions to a protected outsider's previously reachable ground area. This is deliberately limited to a finite orthogonal level ground plane, not flying, elevation, portals or mandatory growth. |
| Memory | The invoking Oracle and their immutable snapshot allies retain only facts individually perceived, experienced or received. Retained memories accumulate across loops. Enemy player characters receive no special knowledge; no hidden roster or Director facts enter memory automatically. |

## What the agreed rules mean at the table

These examples explain the reviewed boundaries. They do not enable the full ability before its remaining integrations are complete.

| Situation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| At initiative, an ally has25HP. Later they fall to3HP and spend8RP. Time Loop succeeds. | They return to25HP, limited by their current legal maximum. The8RP remain spent. Their snapshot encounter allowances return where the source explicitly permits it. |
| The same ally's legal maximum has fallen to20 because a conserved source changed. | They return to20HP. The reduction is temporal normalization, not damage or healing, and creates neither Wounds nor resource triggers. A structural progression change without its adapter instead makes the restore unavailable. |
| An ally began with a6-point Soul Cage shield, later lost it, and the original grant remains valid. | The same shield returns with its snapshot6 points. The Soul Charge paid for it remains spent. This is not a new cast, grant or recipient offer. |

| A restored enemy dies again after its reward opportunity was already claimed. | That same reward cannot be claimed again. The source opportunity, rather than the new death event, determines whether it was paid. |
| A body part was harvested after initiative and still exists as somebody else's item. | The generic restore is unavailable: it cannot duplicate the body part or take away the current owner's item. A specifically reviewed reconciliation would be required. |
| An ally saw a hidden passage in the discarded timeline; another ally never learned about it. | The witness can retain that memory if eligible through the invoking Oracle's snapshot alliance. The other ally receives no automatic knowledge. The witness can tell them normally. |

An unavailable restore spends neither the Reaction nor the long-rest entitlement. The Director needs a complete, legal proposed state before resolving the ability; unresolved source interactions cannot be waived by calling a snapshot complete.

The minimum seventeen-domain review is not complete. Seven major integrations are unimplemented: actual concentration/transformation callbacks; Druid form and conserved recharge clocks; creature lifecycle/corpse/persistent assets; device lifecycle/stock/commands; remaining structures, Choir and control lifecycles; the complete FeatWorld; and source-qualified control/healing pulses. For example, the external concentration map is a dependency projection, not the callback-bearing live concentration adapter.

`TemporalKernel.support_report()` reports that limit. `playable_plan()` always rejects until the full implementation and independent review exist. `kernel_plan()` is a development fixture interface, not a replacement for the complete Oracle feature. The host must disclose every active integration. A supplied unsupported holder rejects preflight; an empty registration is not a certificate that a real game scene is complete.

`TemporalHealingCommitLedger` can be passed as the one canonical healing ledger to existing helpers. Its canonical return IDs preserve `FeatWorld.commit_healing` removal semantics, while its historical consumption tokens are iteration-qualified. Capture/preflight validate the live registry independently of `register()`: exact source/identity/absolute clock, canonical owner/target, boolean availability, and matching consumption-token/event history. # Time Loop: forms and concentration

**Source policies discussed and the 59-check operation-history layer jointly reviewed. Parent restoration remains unimplemented; full Time Loop remains unavailable.**

The [actual parent conference](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_PARENT_BOUNDARIES.md) applies the [twelve conservation decisions](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_WORLD_BOUNDARIES.md) to the current Druid and transformation helpers. The [form rules](FORM_TEMP_HP_PLAYTEST.md) and [transformation spell rules](TRANSFORMATION_SPELL_PLAYTEST.md) retain authority over ordinary play. This is a temporal overlay, not a new form, spell, class benefit or release of the full Oracle ability.

## Decisions for play

| Situation | Proposed restoration under the discussed policy |
|---|---|
| A participant's snapshot Polymorph ended after concentration failed; its original deadline is still future | Restore the same cast, link and original concentration callback together, if every source dependency is legal. No new cast, payment, save or entry event. |
| The participant now concentrates on a different post-snapshot source | Retire that later source only after projecting its complete consequences. Its RP and finite uses stay spent. Unsupported effects or protected outsider consequences make the rewind unavailable. |
| An outsider supplied the snapshot concentration | The exact original slot must still be current. The outsider's slot, resources and body do not rewind. |
| Mass Polymorph affects a participant and a nonparticipant | The first parent implementation may accept only the still-current exact shared cast/slot with every outsider link unchanged. If concentration ended or replacement would change an outsider, reject; do not reconstruct a partial cast. |
| The same True Polymorph reached its original stabilization checkpoint after initiative | Retain permanent status and the absence of concentration. Do not turn it back into shaping or replay the checkpoint. |
| That stabilized True Polymorph was later dispelled or replaced | It may return as the same permanent link only when the later ending is rewindable, physical lineage remains unique, and current gear, enrollment, suppression and geometry all reconcile. A protected current replacement prevents restoration. |
| Druid form F was legally renewed at second 600 to second 1200; rewind occurs at second 601 | Preserve the paid renewal and deadline 1200. The shift stays spent. Never set the deadline back to 600 or forward to 1201. The extension belongs only to F. |
| F ended after that renewal | Restore F with deadline 1200 only if the ending is rewindable and current time is still strictly before 1200. A conserved external ending or expired endpoint blocks it. |
| A form special was unused at snapshot but used afterward | Its same-instance local permission may return. Current Surges, rest uses, recharge state and other required costs still govern actual use. An exhausted global resource cannot be bypassed. |
| Broodmother is restored | Its entry-only spawn window stays closed. Restore creates no entry event. |
| Bear's entry shield had 12 points at snapshot and was later lost | Restore the same grant to 12 only if the original form dependency is valid. Current Buffer Reserve stays spent; no new shield offer occurs. |
| Mooncursed ended after giving an ally its Howl shield | That shield follows its original recipient long-rest endpoint, independently of the form. Restore uses the same grant and no new Surge or reserve allocation. |
| A new iteration gives the Druid a genuine regular start | Feed the next real global regular marker to the existing owner recharge clock once. A tick occurs only if its conserved due marker is actually due. Rewind itself calls no clock method. |
| An outside-origin Shapechange exists at snapshot | The first genuine owner regular turn in the new iteration is later than the original cast. A switch still costs its Bonus Action, requires a different legal profile, and occurs at most once in that authenticated turn. |
| A hostile transformation's damage-triggered repeat save was used only after snapshot | Preserve the old event history. The first qualifying positive normal-HP damage in the new iteration-round may allow its ordinary repeat save. Restore itself rolls nothing. |
| Druid Refrain, remembered spell or Dissonance changed after snapshot | Keep the current shared cadence values. Restoring a form neither clears them nor restores older values. A real paid shift's earlier Refrain clear stays recorded. |
| A required snapshot form expired with no valid renewal or permanent stabilization | Reject restoration requiring that anatomy. There is no generic permission to substitute base anatomy while keeping selected old movement, gear or shield benefits. |
| An otherwise live spell form is currently suppressed | Preserve the actual external suppression, express the required operative anatomy and preflight geometry together. Suppression does not grant a new duration or recapture equipment. |

The notebook [confirmed the Action-budget clarification](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_PARENT_CADENCE_CLARIFICATION.md): snapshot turn allowances return with outstanding Time Loop Reaction debts overlaid; past event history and finite RP/rest expenditures remain conserved. No parent implementation may introduce an additional Action refund or charge while retiring a cast.

## Newly specified temporal rules

These are explicit provisional design additions rather than recovered historical rules:

- Participant concentration restoration reuses the exact retained original slot/callback and the whole original source relationship. Equivalent text IDs or freshly built callbacks are insufficient.
- A post-snapshot dispel or replacement can be undone for a uniquely preserved permanent True Polymorph when the ending and its dependencies are rewindable. Its permanent world checkpoint never becomes a shaping phase again.
- Same-instance Druid renewal needs historical evidence of the legal renewal and payment. A changed expiry field alone does not prove a paid extension.
- Outside-origin Shapechange has an explicit cast-origin record with its real cast identity and time, distinct from an invented encounter turn zero.
- Druid's current Refrain, remembered spell and Dissonance are conserved casting economy/history. They are not form-local permissions restored from the snapshot.

Future genuine events modify that current cadence only under their existing rules. There is no new generic short-rest Dissonance reset here. The frozen common rules identify Retune, long rest, the limited meditation option, qualified idle turns and Grounding; class-specific vents retain their exact source requirements. The temporal bridge does not broaden those recovery permissions or implement every class's cadence hooks.

## Required source history

A complete parent adapter must retain the original cast/form ID, actual creation marker, exact owner/targets, original source procedure, original concentration slot/callback where applicable, and original physical lineage. It must also record renewal, stabilization and ending events with their real markers and causes. A current `state` or `expiry` field cannot establish that history by itself.

A renewal record identifies F, the prior endpoint, the new endpoint, the actual event and its source-qualified payment. A level-20 zero-shift renewal remains a real authorized renewal event. A new form cannot borrow another instance's extension. A stabilization record identifies the original True link and its resolved checkpoint even if that link was subsequently dispelled. An ending record must distinguish a rewindable participant event from a protected external or persistent change.

Retained past events never become new payment, reward, entry, cast, healing or save events. Local permission views use iteration-qualified keys while their original event histories remain intact.

## Implementation order and acceptance cases

The first implementation layer is `tools/temporal_parent_history.py`: an observational journal over the actual Druid and transformation objects. The notebook's [initial 38-method review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_PARENT_HISTORY_REVIEW.md) identified four evidence gaps: unbound stats/prices, unobserved finite economy, unrelated lifecycle changes recorded as legitimate operations, and incorrect outside-cast labels. The [exact repair](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/CODEX_TEMPORAL_PARENT_HISTORY_REPAIR.md) passed 55 checks; the notebook [confirmed those four repairs and found two further gaps](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_PARENT_HISTORY_REPAIR_REVIEW.md). The [subsequent exact fix](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/CODEX_TEMPORAL_PARENT_HISTORY_TIME_PIN_REPAIR.md) binds current query time and append-only references, passes [59 checks](TEMPORAL_PARENT_HISTORY_VALIDATION.json), and has [actual notebook closure](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_PARENT_HISTORY_CLOSURE.md). All six evidence findings are confirmed repaired within this history-only scope. Its [current status manifest](TEMPORAL_PARENT_HISTORY_REVIEW_STATUS.json) binds the submitted files and keeps the wider integration open.

The candidate binds current character stats and ordinary spell quotes, watches Druid-owned finite resources/rests/recharge, restricts lifecycle evidence to the actual operation and requested identities, and distinguishes outside events from real outside casts. A save callback cannot introduce unrelated parent changes. Shared casting cadence remains current; this does not implement all class casting hooks or authorize discounts/free copies. Shield-grant history remains the responsibility of the canonical Buffer adapter.

This layer begins observing before source creation; it cannot reconstruct old history from current state. `valid_form_deadline()` establishes a recorded endpoint, not permission to reactivate the form. `permanent_link()` establishes a historical True checkpoint, not permission to override a later protected ending. Ordinary source access, geometry and authoritative save results still come from the host and existing helpers. A failed native operation that already changed observed state blocks further temporal admission pending host reconciliation. The journal does not roll back a committed cast or replay its save.

No parent restore transaction is implemented by this layer. The [reference-transport extension](TEMPORAL_REFERENCE_TRANSACTION_REVIEW_STATUS.json) is now jointly reviewed with 15 new checks and 207 regression checks. It carries exact original FormInstance and concentration slot/callback references in the same atomic transaction, including rollback. It certifies identity transport only. Full source planning, dependency reconciliation, temporal turn wrappers and kernel integration remain required below.

The [field inventory](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/TEMPORAL_PARENT_STATE_INVENTORY.json) accounts for 85 actual fields across nine holder types and links all 26 Druid profiles. It is an engineering checklist, not runtime validation. In particular, Druid reserves created by `_refill()` are included, not just constructor fields.

The candidate `tools/temporal_parent_watches.py` now watches the complete currently supported parent graph for changes between preparation and commit. Its [11 local checks](TEMPORAL_PARENT_WATCH_VALIDATION.json) exercise actual renewal, concentration ending, gear loss, resource and life changes, historical forms, rests and reference replacement. Independent review is pending with the complete planner. An attached creature graph remains explicitly unsupported by this candidate. These watches grant no restoration permission.

The [ordinary body and equipment conference](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_BODY_EQUIPMENT_CONFERENCE.md) found a prerequisite: native Druid operations do not yet update the shared Body, inventory custody or geometry. The subsequent [source reconciliation](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_CARRYING_RECONCILIATION.md) and [final manuscript confirmation](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_BODY_FINAL_AND_ABJURATION_CONFERENCE.md) now establish the [authored body and carrying candidate](BODY_EQUIPMENT_PLAYTEST.md): Tiny subcells, preserved base weight, actual custody, separate carrying quantities and fixed meld-chain ceilings. 1. Bind canonical Core life, BufferLedger, concentration, Druid, physical inventory and persistent enrollment references. Prove every active source and child is disclosed.
2. Preserve source creation/renewal/stabilization/ending receipts and the original concentration references. Validate their history before taking a snapshot or charging a rewind.

7. Exercise real later concentration endings, due recharge starts, form specials, repeat saves and paid switches against those same restored objects. A later ordinary event must reach the intended source exactly once.

Required adverse cases include replaced canonical objects; same-ID callback replacement; ended mixed-roster concentration; transferred or destroyed melded equipment; competing persistent sponsor slots; fabricated renewal/stabilization receipts; expired form children; exhausted Surge with restored local permission; Broodmother spawn replay; a due versus not-yet-due recharge at unchanged world time; duplicate regular markers; malformed collections; and a source mutation between preflight and commit. ## Agreed temporal behavior

| State | Temporal rule |
| --- | --- |
| Explicit source/target regular endpoints | Restore remaining logical progress with authentic new-iteration regular markers. World elapsed time does not move backward, and restoration creates no marker event. |
| Current actual-turn endings | Remain attached to the actual application turn. The initiative-start snapshot has no active turn; a pending in-turn attachment there is invalid. Outside-turn +6-second endpoints retain their absolute deadline. |
| Outside-origin pulse schedules | Keep their original virtual markers and absolute deadlines. Entering initiative or using Time Loop does not restart them. Origin must be recorded explicitly. |

Aura, net, form, serum and creature children require their actual parent adapters. Hypermutation's floor is systemic parent state, not a hostile slow. |
| Guiding Bolt's Star mark | Restore its two separate entitlements. Keep the same mark identity and monotonic attack-token history; pending attacks block capture and preflight. |
| Wrathful Brand | Restore the separate owner/ally riders and snapshot timed parent. No new damage, healing or save event occurs at restore. |
| One-shot riders | Use exact parent/application/source/component identities and a finite trigger table. Vein Cutter consumes on its qualifying attack hit; Crippling Lash specifically requires a weapon hit. Omen Reader's once/encounter attack adjustment is distinct from the resulting timed star-ash. |
| Divine Judgment reflection | Retain historical actual-turn consumption. A genuinely new iteration turn can qualify, including a separately authenticated extra turn. Ordinary repeat saves and expiry still use regular markers. |

| Eternal Bloom | Preserve the original missing-HP capture and shares. Restore only snapshot installment availability; retain old consumption history. Do not grow the reserve from later damage. Its survival floor is separate. |

| Native healing | One evaluated opportunity at a genuine regular start during a real encounter. Decline, ineligibility or unavailable payment loses that start opportunity. Extra turns and downtime create no tick. A new iteration can supply a new genuine start, with current RP/reserves. |

**Resource-output conservation:** Transcendent Meditation's second pulse can supply1Ki only once for the same effect instance. Sacred Chant's third pulse can supply1Conviction only once for that instance. Reaching the occurrence while capped or while the whole effect is suppressed still consumes that resource opportunity. Healing may later replay under an authorized restored source without generating the same resource again. A never-reached opportunity remains eligible. Restoration itself grants neither resource.

For example, a Monk receives the second pulse's1Ki, then spends it. Rewinding to a snapshot where that pulse was pending can permit its healing again when legally due, but it cannot return that same1Ki. Sacred Chant uses the same conservation rule for Conviction.

The immutable snapshot is at initiative start. A source first created afterward is not silently added to that snapshot. An origin label cannot manufacture preexisting pulse state. Any logical-clock restoration must demonstrate that the actual source instance was already present in the captured state.

The conference's maintenance wording is read with its express instruction not to reopen ordinary mechanics: an early failed ordinary turn-window payment remains pending until the source's real turn-end deadline. Exact-due paid sequences/windows end immediately on failed upkeep. The notebook explicitly [confirmed this distinction and immutable snapshot membership](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_PULSE_BRIDGE_CLOSURE.md). No currently supplied pulse profile needs a fabricated at-initiative creation exception; native passive abilities instead await their future genuine regular-start events.

## Current code and checks

`tools/temporal_control_playtest_rules.py` currently implements two limited bridges:

- `CanonicalPulseWallet` lets existing pulse helpers spend the real actor Wallet's RP/Bonus Action and the canonical Scheduler's RC. It owns no duplicate balances and rejects changed aliases before spending.
- `ConservedPulseOutputs` wraps actual `PulseSeries.resolve()` calls for the two resource-producing profiles. It retains unique occurrence IDs and conserved instance/index/component opportunities; it replaces the helper's raw Ki flag with the guarded allowance. Suppressed or capped resolved occurrences cannot be banked. Sacred Chant cannot generate Conviction outside a real encounter.

## Object damage and Sunder

These are **new mundane object procedures** completing the Core Sunder interface. A target must be one actual separately tracked object or explicitly modeled separable component. Naming an armor strap, pin, lace, hinge or seam does not create a cheaper independent target. Construct joints remain subject to the creature's actual stat block.

Sunder uses an actual legal weapon attack against one perceived reachable object/component, consuming one attack when taking the Attack Action. It grants no extra attack or free damage to a wearer. The attacker cannot target a hidden component through a creature or solid obstruction. Against worn/held gear, target AC is the higher of the material AC and wearer's current AC. Unattended gear uses material AC. Ordinary attack eligibility and printed object-target exclusions still apply.

Worn/carried inventory is never damaged merely because its creature is hit. An attack, spell or hazard damages equipment only if its actual rule expressly targets/includes objects, structures, carried gear or that item. Sunder never also damages the wearer unless another source expressly says so.

| Load-bearing material | AC |
|---|---:|
| Cloth, paper, rope | 11 |
| Glass, crystal | 13 |
| Wood, leather | 15 |
| Stone | 17 |
| Iron, steel | 19 |

For a mixed object, establish its dominant load-bearing material before damage. Do not retroactively select a material after the attack roll.

| Mundane object | Maximum structural HP |
|---|---:|
| Tiny vial or letter | 1 |
| Tool, weapon or focus | 5 |
| Ordinary shield | 10 |
| Tower shield | 15 |
| Light armor | 10 |
| Medium armor | 15 |
| Heavy armor | 20 |
| Ordinary chest or door | 20 |
| Cart | 30 |
| Targeted rope segment | 5 |
| Targeted chain segment | 10 |

Large-sized wearable/item generic HP doubles; Crude armor's half-HP rule then applies. Specific source/card durability wins, including a net's AC 10/5 slashing destruction rule and Tinker gnome devices' AC 5/HP 1. The ordinary buckler is a shield using 10 generic HP. Objects outside a listed or genuinely comparable category need an actual assigned profile before targeted durability resolution; no automatic structure or artifact certification is implied.

Objects are immune to poison and psychic damage unless an exact rule says otherwise. Establish physical damage compatibility before rolling: a sword cannot chop a liquid. Do not invent retroactive resistances. Use ordinary attack damage and applicable weapon properties; creature-only conditions and resource triggers do not become object-eligible.

At zero structural HP, the object is **Broken** and loses usable AC, weapon, focus, tool or other functional benefits. It still exists, occupies its hand/slot/container and retains mass until dropped, removed or repaired. Broken armor does not disappear. No negative HP, duplicated loot, automatic explosion, passive regeneration or repair from ordinary rest. Magic items/artifacts need their own durability; no mundane default is assigned to unresolved magical gear. True Polymorph's independently excluded-object rules still apply even when an object has HP.

A Broken item grants none of its positive usable benefits, but remains physically worn, held or strapped until removed. It continues to occupy its hand/slot and contribute weight/Load, and retains physical drawbacks from still wearing or carrying it: applicable don/doff requirements, armor Stealth disadvantage, STR-minimum movement penalty and nonproficiency consequences. A Broken shield grants no AC bonus but still occupies its actual hand/forearm until doffed. A specific source may state otherwise.

## Material identity, consumption and substitution

Keep the exact recipe ID and component occurrence. Global material names alone are insufficient: 143 embedded names have different tier/price/weight variants. Record identity as the recipe component's name, tier, category, properties, unit weight, unit value and source occurrence. Quantity belongs to the inventory lot, not the identity. Preserve component IDs where supplied; none are silently merged or normalized to a cheaper same-name material. The 2-gp crafting Crystal Vial and 5-gp equipment Vial remain distinct records unless an explicit compatibility/substitution ruling is recorded.

An exact recipe component's stored numeric `tier` remains part of that component's identity and may be compared for that recipe's explicit substitution requirements even when the stored number exceeds 6. This does not extend the generic V4 material-tier ladder or generic harvesting entitlement beyond Tier VI. A Tier 7–10 stored component therefore receives no generic harvest DC, public availability, rarity right or substitution source merely from that number; it requires its actual recipe/source acquisition procedure or another separately reviewed rule.

**Source:** substitutions require the relevant properties and tier unless the recipe names an irreplaceable ingredient. **Completion:** before spending materials, a substitute must satisfy each replaced unit's tier (equal or higher), all required functional properties and role, compatible physical form, and at least its required amount. The Director records the mapping and its actual unit quantities/weights/value. Higher price alone is not compatibility; a higher-tier component does not increase the result tier, quantity or effect. A unique named core cannot be replaced under this general permission. Do not repeatedly change the substitution after observing the outcome.

Reserve consumed quantities at the start and deduct them once at resolution or deliberate abandonment. Abandonment after work starts loses consumed inputs with no product/recovery roll; actual nonconsumed tools and intact independently stored unused supplies remain. Ingredients left outside the reservation remain usable but cannot also fund another order. Return only the exact quantities authorized by Masterwork or ordinary failure, never both for one result. No recovery from a Mishap. Component `consumed=false` returns its full reserved quantity; role=tool is not itself a consumed flag.

Nineteen source component rows have role=tool and consumed=true. Treat these as incorporated parts in those exact recipes, not the separately required reusable toolkit; retain their flags until individual recipe review. A focusing lens incorporated into a device is not a reusable station lens. The work order must supply both if it needs both. Never 'repair' all role=tool rows to nonconsumed in bulk.

Ordinary failure recovery uses each identity's physical units: an indivisible organ, lens, bottle or crystal rounds down to whole units; explicitly divisible bulk reagent can be recorded to 0.01 source units. Recovery never creates money. For example, four ordinary indivisible non-catalyst vials return one; one irreplaceable catalyst returns zero. These recovered lots retain their age and identity. A failed batch cannot be salvaged again for another automatic 25%.
